messages:
Kenji: Morning — quick async standup (3-line): what I did / blockers / today
Marta L: Did: wired up extra routeguard unit tests for the weight-based routing change. Found a flaky test, pushed a fix.
Marta L: Blocker: need logs from dedicated-gw-prod for one failing scenario (asking infra for access).
Marta L: Today: finish the canary config PR and add a test matrix for small / large payloads.
Ajay: Did: rolled token-issuer image to staging and ran soak for 2h. Saw a thin spike of 429s — looks correlated with bursty background jobs.
Ajay: Blocker: don't have confidence in current burst window. Want to try lowering burst and enabling soft-backoff for consumers.
Ajay: Today: opening a tiny config PR (route-policy) and will run a 1h canary with 5% traffic. Ping me if you see token-related 401s.
Julia: Did: reviewed Kenji's auth JWT rotation changes, left 2 nits around comments and one concurrency hint.
Julia: Blocker: none.
Julia: Today: will approve once the small concurrency guard is added, then queue for canary.
Kenji: Did: finished the routing policy rebase and fixed the deadlock in cache invalidation.
Kenji: Blocker: need a second +1 on the performance regression test before cutting the canary.
Kenji: Today: merge routing PR once Julia approves, kick off canary at ~10:30 PST, start 30% -> 60% -> 100% ramp if metrics look good.
deploy-bot: deploy: canary job started for commit d9f4a2 (route-policy + token-bump) — see: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/8721
Marta L: quick note — adding a tiny smoke check to avoid the flaky unit failing only in CI. Patch in the PR.
Ajay: ping Kenji: PTAL at my route-policy diff, especially the burst -> backoff section.
Kenji: On it, will review in 15m. If all green I'll :shipit: after Julia's approval.
Julia: Approved the concurrency patch. Left one inline nit but not blocking.
Kenji: Thanks — sequencing as: (1) merge tests, (2) deploy canary, (3) run traffic-shift script, (4) monitor token error rate and latencies.
Marta L: FYI adding tiny logging to capture the failing header shape so infra can correlate with client.
Ajay: If we still see 429s on canary, I suggest we temporarily reduce burst on the affected route to 200/s and add client-side jitter.
Kenji: noted. If canary shows >0.5% 429 increase we'll auto-roll back.
Julia: I'll watch the dashboards. Add me to the PagerDuty rota for the window.
Kenji: wrap — thanks all. If anything urgent ping me @kenji or drop an epic in #incidents.
